rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for committing to do something or assuring someone that you will do it.

example.english: I promise you I’ll definitely help you move tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我應承你聽日一定幫你搬屋。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jing1 sing4 nei5 ting1 jat6 jat1 ding6 bong1 nei5 bun1 uk1

rows.note: Use this when the promise is emphatic and carries the force of a guarantee.

example.english: I promise I’ll get the report in tonight.
example.traditional: 我保證份報告今晚一定交到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 bou2 zing3 fan6 bou3 gou3 gam1 maan5 jat1 ding6 gaau1 dou3

rows.note: Use this specifically for making a solemn oath or vow rather than an ordinary promise.

example.english: I promise I didn’t take your book—I swear.
example.jyutping: ngo5 faat3 sai6 mou5 lo2 gwo3 nei5 bun2 syu1

rows.note: Use 承諾 as the all-purpose noun for a pledge or promise that someone makes.

example.english: They finally kept their promise to me.
example.traditional: 佢終於兌現咗對我嘅承諾。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zung1 jyu1 deoi3 jin6 zo2 deoi3 ngo5 ge3 sing4 nok6

rows.note: Use 潛質 when promise means talent or likelihood of future success in a person.

example.english: This young man has great promise and will succeed sooner or later.
example.traditional: 呢個後生仔好有潛質，遲早會成功。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hau6 saang1 zai2 hou2 jau5 cim4 zat1 ci4 zou2 wui5 sing4 gung1

rows.traditional: 睇 A 個勢會 B
rows.jyutping: tai2 A go3 sai3 wui5 B
rows.note: Use this colloquial construction when observable signs make an outcome seem likely.

example.english: The way things look now, the signs promise that we’ll win.
example.jyutping: tai2 ji4 gaa1 go3 sai3 wui5 jeng4 bo1 wo3
